filesChanged.change: Added NodeSupersessionKind ("PROVISION_LEVEL" | "DOCUMENT_LEVEL") type. Extended NodeSupersessionRecord with required fields supersessionKind and supersedingOperativeDocumentId. Extended NodeSupersessionIndex with documentLevelSupersededDocuments: Map<string, NodeSupersessionRecord> (documentId-keyed, not nodeId-keyed - see 03-integration-design.json).

buildNodeSupersessionIndex: (1) every pre-existing PROVISION_LEVEL record construction now sets supersessionKind:"PROVISION_LEVEL", supersedingOperativeDocumentId:null (no behavior change). (2) NEW second pass, after the pre-existing per-provision loop: for each entry whose state.operativeDocument.status==="RESOLVED" and whose own baseDocumentId is in predecessorDocumentIds, composes a DOCUMENT_LEVEL record (using the already-computed OperativeDocumentResolution - never a second version-chain algorithm) into the new documentLevelSupersededDocuments map. getNodeSupersessionStatus: NEW RULE 1 check (documentId-keyed lookup against documentLevelSupersededDocuments) inserted before the pre-existing per-node supersededByNodeId lookup - returns KNOWN_SUPERSEDED with full provenance (which document is now operative, which direct edge/effect/date superseded this one) whenever it fires; falls through to 100%-unchanged pre-existing behavior otherwise. EMPTY_SUPERSESSION_INDEX updated additively (new empty Map, inert).

testFixupsReason: These 4 files hand-construct NodeSupersessionIndex/NodeSupersessionRecord object literals directly (rather than going through buildNodeSupersessionIndex). Making supersessionKind/supersedingOperativeDocumentId/documentLevelSupersededDocuments REQUIRED (not optional) fields was a deliberate design choice - it forces every construction site to make an explicit, correct choice rather than silently defaulting, and TypeScript's own compiler caught every site mechanically (6 TS2741/TS2739/TS2345 errors, zero missed). Each site was updated to add supersessionKind:"PROVISION_LEVEL", supersedingOperativeDocumentId:null (matching their own pre-existing provision-level intent) and documentLevelSupersededDocuments:new Map() (empty, matching their own pre-existing lack of whole-document-supersession setup). No test's own assertions or behavior were changed - purely additive object-literal fields.
designIterationLog: No design-iteration surprises this round (unlike the prior pre-unseen-classifier-remediation session's own 19-test-regression false start) - the consumer-inventory pass (02-consumer-inventory.json) done BEFORE implementation correctly predicted zero D-classification consumers and identified the two exhaustive Record<NodeSupersessionStatus,...> maps up front, which is exactly why the KNOWN_SUPERSEDED-reuse design was chosen instead of a new status literal. The only friction was mechanical (four hand-built test fixtures needing the new required record fields), fully enumerated by the TypeScript compiler itself.

postImplementationTypeScriptCheck.result: Exactly the same 6 pre-existing baseline errors (00-baseline.json), zero new.
